The Later Yan page, after the Western Yan campaign of 394 and the annexation of Shanxi: "Then, he sent his generals to capture Shandong from the Eastern Jin dynasty, bringing the state to its peak." The sentence has no year of its own, so 394 is the page's sequence (confidence 2); the page also says Later Yan had recovered its old territory "in Liaoning, Hebei, Shaanxi, Shandong and Henan by 394". The Murong Chui page dates the Western Yan conquest to winter 393 and does not mention Shandong. Mirrors western-jin /ledger/42 (394 loss to later-yan). notes: Cliopatria's Later Yan row 387..409 starts three years late (384) and ends on the right year if the Later Yan infobox (6 November 409) is followed; the Later Yan page's own text ends it in 407 when Feng Ba 'replaced' Murong Yun, and the Northern Yan page dates its own start '407 or 409', so the 407-409 years belong to both. The Cliopatria 407 Later Yan shape is the same set of cells as its Northern Yan 410 shape. The 395-401 shape (Hebei 64 %, Shandong 91 %) holds the pre-Wei-invasion empire for seven years; the pages show it gone by 397-398, so 397-401 is a new keyframe with the 402 remnant. The stray bbox (82.9 E, 51 N) is five cells of noise. The Later Yan page gives no infobox area, so no comparison with the 503 k km2 maximum was possible. Not settled (page budget: Later Yan, Western Yan, Canhe Slope, Northern Yan, Goguryeo, plus Northern Wei and Former Qin pages opened for siblings): Later Yan's actual extent in 384-386 and its hold on Shandong and Liaodong in 387-394; Murong Sheng's and Murong Xi's Goguryeo wars (the Goguryeo page has nothing on 400, 404, 405); Murong De's Southern Yan (its dossier belongs to another batch); the border with Southern Yan. Counterparts without a dossier: zhai-wei (Zhai Wei, Dingling, 388-392, Huatai), and the Dingling rebels of 384 (Zhai Bin). Gazetteer: all names resolve (Luoyang, Baoding, Anyang; regions Liaodong). [ea-03-c fix, 2026-10-19, after the review: (1) Shandong is no longer held 385-393: keyframes 385, 387 and 390 minus Shandong and a 394 gain from western-jin on the Later Yan page's sequence (confidence 2); (2) the Shanxi land stays in the 395-396 keyframe and goes to the Wei in a 396 loss from the Murong Bao page (confidence 2; the page says the attack and the governor's flight, not the hold); (3) the capital Longcheng (Chaoyang) is added to keyframes 397-409 as a 60 km disc; (4) the Goguryeo contest is split: 385 alone, and 400-406 for Gwanggaeto's wars (the reviewer asked for 400-404; the Gwanggaeto page has Later Yan attacking Liaodong again in 405 and 406, so 406 is the last battle; the Liaodong loss stays at 404 on the Later Yan page). Disagreements between pages: the Murong Chui page dates the end of Western Yan to winter 393, the Later Yan and Western Yan pages to 394 (394 kept); the Murong Bao page glosses Longcheng as modern Jinzhou, the Later Yan page and this dossier use Chaoyang. Still open: northern-wei needs the matching 396 gain of Bing Province and the Shandong 394 gain needs no mirror beyond western-jin /ledger/42; Liaoning and Liaodong before 394 are undated.]
